$comment: Golden world-space UI geometry, read by BOTH engines: SexyBiscuit.Tests/UiWorldTests.cs and html5/tests/uiWorld.test.js. Every expectation here was derived by hand rather than recorded from a run, so the fixture pins the arithmetic and not whatever the code happened to do on the day. This is the only check that can see the two engines' trigonometry drifting apart: a canvas on a wall is all basis vectors and ray intersections, and no regex over the other engine's source could ever compare them. Each case builds a basis from `canvas` and `camera`, then either asserts the basis vectors, or fires `ray` at it and asserts the canvas point it lands on -- or that it misses.

cases.name: a ray down the plane's normal lands in the middle of the canvas
cases.why: The simplest true statement about the whole system. If this is wrong nothing else can be right.

cases.name: world up is canvas up, so a hit above centre reads as a smaller canvas Y
cases.why: The one axis flip in the whole feature. Canvas Y grows downwards and the quad's Y does not, and getting this backwards would put every world UI upside down while every test that only checked the centre stayed green.

cases.name: a canvas point put back into the world is where the ray came from
cases.why: canvasToWorld and rayToCanvas are inverses, and a round trip is the cheapest way to say so.

cases.name: a ray parallel to the plane misses it
cases.why: Dividing by a cosine of zero is an infinity, and an infinite canvas coordinate would poison every rectangle test downstream instead of simply missing.

cases.name: a plane behind the pointer misses
cases.why: Without the sign check, a canvas behind the camera takes clicks aimed at the sky in front of it.

cases.name: a hit outside the canvas rectangle is a point but not a distance
cases.why: The point is still wanted -- the layout rejects it on its own -- but the host's nearest-canvas election must not count a canvas the ray sailed past.

cases.name: a billboard in front of the camera faces straight back at it
cases.why: The identity case for the inverse-view basis. Camera down -Z, so the canvas normal is +Z and its axes are the world's.

cases.name: a billboard turns to a camera standing on the +X axis
cases.why: Stand at +X looking towards the origin and your right hand points at -Z. A basis that came out mirrored would still face the camera and would render every label back to front.

cases.name: a vertical billboard ignores how high the camera is
cases.why: The whole point of the mode. A nameplate over a character must not tip backwards when the player looks down at it, so the up axis stays the world's and only the turn about it follows the camera.

cases.name: a vertical billboard turns about Y towards a camera off to the side
cases.why: Same mode, the turn actually happening, and it must agree with the full billboard for a camera at eye level.

cases.name: a plane laid flat takes clicks from a camera looking down at it
cases.why: A UI on a table, which is the case a billboard can never serve. The quarter turn about X puts canvas up along -Z, so walking round the table changes nothing about where a button is.
